description: Two-panel composite of bright-field transmission electron micrographs of deformed Fe–30% Al (at.% Al, weakly DO3-ordered). The LEFT panel is a low-magnification TEM image: a dense, tangled dislocation network with many long, straight, near-screw dislocation segments crossing the field in several directions, together with curved and looped segments and dark band-like patches of residual contrast; a black scale bar is labelled "0.25 µm" and a black arrow points up-left indicating the imaging vector g. The RIGHT panel is a higher-magnification TEM image of the same material showing a much sparser arrangement of dislocation lines, most of them occurring as closely spaced parallel pairs; seven or more such paired segments are arrowed and labelled "d". A wide, gently mottled dark band runs vertically through the field, and the background shows weak, broad fringe-like contrast; the scale bar is labelled "0.1 µm" and the same black arrow marks the imaging vector direction. The caption states the zone axis is near [1 1 1] and the arrowed imaging vector is 1 1 0, and that the paired dislocations marked d are generally dipole segments and loops. The panel pair demonstrates that the deformation substructure of Fe–30% Al consists of straight screw-oriented superdislocations plus numerous edge dislocation dipoles and loops.

observations.observation: The left panel is a low-magnification bright-field TEM micrograph with a printed scale bar reading '0.25 µm'.
The right panel is a higher-magnification bright-field TEM micrograph with a printed scale bar reading '0.1 µm'.
In the right panel, dislocations occur mainly as closely spaced parallel pairs, each marked with the label 'd' (at least seven 'd' labels are visible).
A black arrow indicating the imaging vector g points toward the upper-left in both panels.

The left panel shows a dense dislocation network containing long, straight, near-screw segments crossing the field plus curved and looped segments, whereas the right panel shows a much sparser population.
The caption states the zone axis is near [1 1 1] and that the arrowed imaging vector is 1 1 0.
The caption states that the paired dislocations marked d in the right-hand micrograph are generally dipole segments and loops.

The citing text states that the parallel image pairs visible in Fig. 14 (right) all correspond to short or long dislocation dipole pairs, since the APBI fault energy is high enough that partial separation within the superdislocation is small.

The citing text states that deformation of Fe–30% Al occurs by movement of the same superdislocations composed of 2 × (1/2) 1 1 1 partial dislocations, producing many straight near-screw dislocations as well as many edge dislocation dipoles and loops.
The citing text asserts that the dislocation pairs observed here (and in Fig. 16) are the result of dislocation reactions and do not correspond to the partials of the glissile superdislocations.
The material shown is Fe–30% Al, described in the citing text as weakly DO3 ordered.
Diffraction contrast varies strongly between individual dislocation segments, indicating differing Burgers vectors/screw-edge character under the single g vector used.

subfigures.description: Low-magnification bright-field TEM micrograph of deformed Fe–30% Al showing a dense tangled dislocation network with many long straight near-screw segments, curved/looped dislocations and dark residual-contrast patches; scale bar labelled 0.25 µm; black arrow marks the imaging vector direction.

Higher-magnification bright-field TEM micrograph of the same alloy showing sparse dislocations occurring predominantly as closely spaced parallel pairs, each marked with the letter 'd' (seven or more labels visible); a broad mottled dark band traverses the field vertically; scale bar labelled 0.1 µm; black arrow marks the imaging vector.

unreadable_items: No absolute magnification value is printed; only the scale bars (0.25 µm and 0.1 µm) allow length calibration.
The foil thickness/beam direction outside the stated zone axis near [1 1 1] is not readable from the image.
The exact number of d-labelled dislocation pairs in the left part of the right panel is partly obscured by overlapping contrast.
